header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Time: 16:00-16:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood: Jordan Lee (AE), Maya Patel (SE)
Sable Systems: Evan Chu (Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Director, ML Engineering), Samir Patel (FinOps)
Recording: yes
Shared artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/decks/sable-demo, sample routes CSV (requested)
summary: Quick console tour focused on per-route dashboards, usage analytics, and cost breakdown. Walkthrough of token-level cost, per-route attribution, and recommendations for Dedicated vs Hosted for predictable latency. Customer raised compliance (SOC2/KMS), data residency and FinOps approval questions. Agreed to pilot with representative routes and follow-up pricing + security docs.
topics: KV cache and batching impact on economics
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript: 00:00 Jordan: ok everyone can hear me? good afternoon, thanks for joining — we're excited to walk through the console and the route economics stuff
00:12 Evan: yep loud and clear, thanks for doing this — we've been trying to get our FinOps and platform aligned on inference costs
00:22 Priya: quick thing — our stack is mostly in eu-west and gcp, we run a small self-hosted transformer for latency-sensitive routing, curious how Redwood maps to that
00:35 Maya: thanks Priya, we'll show the per-route view which maps incoming API keys / routes to cost and latency, also how to pin model versions or route traffic to Dedicated pools
01:05 Jordan: agenda — 1) quick console tour (usage analytics, per-route dashboards) 2) cost breakdown and token-level attribution 3) Q&A around security and deployment 4) next steps/pilot
01:28 Samir: sound good — from finance I'm mostly interested in unit economics, what drives token cost variance across routes
01:40 Maya: great — we'll start on the Routes page. heading to the dashboard now — bear with me while I pull up the sample tenant, link shared in chat

02:02 Maya: you can see top routes by spend, and an interactive filter for model, region, and client-id — notice here route 'summarize-docs' has high cost per request because of long sequences and large output tokens
02:30 Evan: hmm that one is chatty — we send large context plus the model replies, is there a way to attribute cost just to the model variant or to the caching layer?

02:45 Maya: yes — we break cost into request tokens, response tokens, and also show potential savings from prefix/KV caching. here's a 'what-if' toggle to simulate enabling prefix cache which drops request-tokens dramatically
03:10 Priya: interesting, that toggle showed a 28% reduction in token cost for that route — is that based on real traffic patterns?

03:22 Maya: it's workload-aware sampling — the console runs a simulated pass using your sample traffic to show estimated savings; of course real numbers vary, but it's a good guide for planning batching/caching
04:00 Jordan: also worth noting quantization profile recommendations — for some routes we suggest an 8-bit quantized variant with small accuracy loss but 40% lower per-token compute costs
04:20 Samir: is that safe for our sensitive models? what about degradation and evals?
04:29 Maya: we integrate quality monitoring — you can pin a set of prompts and compare outputs across model variants with side-by-side diff, and rollback if regressions exceed your threshold
05:01 Evan: client asks about latency; they want sub-100ms p50 for a user-facing route — how do we guarantee?

05:12 Jordan: that's where Dedicated capacity and routing policies come into play — we provision reserved GPU pools and SLO-backed latency targets. console shows historical latency percentiles per route so you can validate
05:40 Priya: can we mix hosted and Dedicated? i.e., burst to hosted when Dedicated saturated?
05:51 Maya: yes — smart routing policies allow fallback to compatible hosted variants; the console visualizes fallback events and their cost/latency impact
06:18 Samir: procurement question — we need audit logs and KMS for keys; what's included in Private offering?

06:28 Jordan: Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control plane in your network, integrates with your KMS/HSM, and we provide detailed audit logs. we also have SOC2 reports and a network architecture doc — i'll send them
06:55 Priya: are there standard connectors for SSO — SAML/Okta?
07:03 Maya: yep SSO, SCIM, RBAC — console supports role-based access to routes and models, and you can see token-level usage per principal
07:25 Evan: back to cost, can you show the per-token cost breakout?

07:34 Maya: switching to Cost detail -> Token breakdown. here each model has a per-token compute cost plus infra surcharge; the console attributes cost to the route by multiplying tokens consumed by the model's cost profile and adding route-level overheads
07:58 Priya: the compute cost column mentions 'kv cache hit rate' — is that real-time?
08:06 Maya: it's sampled, updated hourly. the console will also surface routes with low cache effectiveness and suggest payload redesign or prefix caching
08:28 Evan: are the cost numbers exportable to our billing system? we need CSVs for internal chargeback
08:36 Jordan: yes exports, plus an API you can pull. we'll also send a spreadsheet template that maps routes to accounting tags
09:00 Samir: about pilot — we want to trial 10 routes, two user-facing low-latency, eight high-volume background. timeline?
09:10 Jordan: think 2–3 weeks to set up a test tenant, ingests sample traffic, run a 7-day baseline. pilot kickoff week of Nov 15 works with our schedule
09:35 Maya: i'll flag the route tagging requirements — need route id, sample qps, typical input/output token lengths, and a representative sample CSV
10:00 Priya: on the console UI, can you show the anomaly detection/alerts tied to cost spikes?

10:09 Maya: yes — alerts can be tied to route spend thresholds, token rate increases, or sudden latency regressions. here is an example where a model rollout caused a 3x response token increase and triggered an alert
10:40 Evan: any way to tie that to code changes? we want blame to trace to deploys
10:48 Maya: we ingest optional deployment tags; you can link route changes to your CI/CD tags and the console surfaces associated changes during the timeframe

11:12 Jordan: moving to the 'Optimize' recommendations — console suggests batching windows and a latency budget tradeoff. for batched background routes you can increase batch window to get big cost wins
11:40 Samir: give me a concrete example — numbers please

11:45 Maya: sure — for route 'nlp-enrich' we observed p90 latency tolerable at 800ms; increasing batch window from 5ms to 25ms increased throughput and reduced cost per token by ~32% in the simulation
12:20 Priya: are those simulations conservative? we worry about overcommitting to batch settings that break SLAs
12:29 Maya: the console sim uses your real latency distribution and lets you set max acceptable p99. it will only recommend batch sizes that keep p99 under your threshold
13:05 Evan: security follow-up — need a copy of SOC2 + network architecture for our security review
13:12 Jordan: noted — i'll attach SOC2, encryption at rest docs, and the public network diagram. also will include the Private deployment checklist
13:35 Samir: procurement needs rough cost bands: if we put these 10 routes on Dedicated versus Hosted what's the delta monthly?

13:44 Jordan: we'll run a model-specific cost projection and send a side-by-side; ballpark for your traffic sample Dedicated reduces tail latency and can lower unit costs depending on CPU/GPU mix — we'll quantify
14:10 Priya: can you show the rollout UI for a canary A/B?
14:18 Maya: here — you can create a rollout, set weights per model variant, and observe delta in accuracy/cost/latency in real time. there's also an automatic rollback rule
14:50 Evan: what about multi-region residency? we need EU-only for some PII workflows
14:58 Jordan: Private deployments can be in your region; hosted — we also have eu-west endpoints and region routing policies. console flags routes with residency requirements
15:25 Priya: ok that's helpful. anything else on billing tags and chargeback?
15:33 Maya: you can assign tags to routes, teams, and projects; the billing export groups by tag. also per-token breakdown by tag if you need drilldown
15:58 Samir: last question — competitors we evaluated had simpler pricing but less visibility. can Redwood show historical regressions tied to a model change?
16:06 Maya: yes — quality monitoring links prompt-set based regressions to a timestamp and model id so you can correlate to model rollouts
16:30 Evan: ok let's recap — Jordan to send pricing + SOC2/docation, Maya to share console recording + tenant link, Sable to provide route CSV and approve pilot dates. are we all aligned?
16:45 Priya: yes aligned, i'll own the route CSV and sample traffic
16:50 Samir: i'll confirm budget and procurement timeline
16:54 Jordan: perfect, thanks everyone — we'll get those artifacts over in the next 48 hours
16:58 (call ends)
